record.title: China's CAC announces a two-month campaign against misleading military content, including AI-generated fabrications
record.summary: A Chinese-language notice dated October 12 and published by the Cyberspace Administration of China on October 15 announces a two-month, multi-agency campaign against improper marketing and sensationalized military-related content online. The ten listed categories include AI-generated fake military dramas, stories and videos. The notice directs authorities to require platform review and cleanup, but reports no implementation results, AI-specific technical requirements or measured effects.
organizations: Ministry of Veterans Affairs of the People's Republic of China
Central Military Commission Political Work Department
Central Military Commission Political and Legal Affairs Commission

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The official notice dated October 12 and posted October 15 announces a two-month coordinated campaign and enumerates ten categories of military-related misleading marketing or sensationalized content; one category explicitly covers fabricated military stories, short dramas and videos generated with AI.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The notice directs local cyber and veterans-affairs authorities and military units to coordinate with platforms, strengthen content review and remove material within the listed categories.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice does not establish implementation fidelity, enforcement counts, platform-level technical measures, reduced prevalence of AI-generated fabrications or downstream public effects.

evidence_gaps.description: No public evidence of implementing platform instructions, review changes or campaign enforcement outcomes was available in the notice.
The notice supplies no baseline or follow-up measure for prevalence of AI-generated military fabrications or platform removals.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as announced, the campaign places AI-generated military fabrications within a coordinated two-month enforcement effort involving national and local cyber, veterans-affairs and military bodies. This is a meaningful policy signal for synthetic-media governance, while the notice alone does not establish implementation or outcomes.
limitations: This is an official policy notice describing intended enforcement; no implementation evidence or outcomes are reported.
The notice lists AI-generated fabricated military stories and videos as one of ten categories; it does not state an AI-specific detection standard or technical obligation.
No enforcement counts, platform-level compliance audit, baseline or follow-up prevalence measure is provided.
The document's stated date is October 12, while the CAC page publication timestamp is October 15, 2026.
organizations: Ministry of Veterans Affairs of the People's Republic of China
Central Military Commission Political Work Department
Central Military Commission Political and Legal Affairs Commission

The ten listed categories include AI-generated fake military dramas, stories and videos. technical.claimed_result: Authorities state that the campaign will tighten platform responsibility, remove specified misleading or improper military-related content and publicize representative cases. No results are reported in this announcement.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Chinese notice documents the campaign's stated dates, participating bodies, ten target categories and requested platform cleanup. This confirms the published policy text, not its implementation or effect.
technical.mechanism: A two-month campaign coordinates cyber-administration and veterans-affairs agencies with military political-work and political-legal bodies; authorities are directed to coordinate with platforms, strengthen review and remove specified military-related marketing and sensationalized content, including a listed category of AI-generated fabrications.
technical.regime: A two-month campaign announced in October 2026 by national Chinese cyber-administration, veterans-affairs and military bodies, with implementation assigned through local authorities and online platforms. The notice includes ten categories and identifies AI-generated fake military stories, dramas and videos in one category.
technical.reproducibility: The policy document is publicly accessible in Chinese. Its implementation cannot be independently assessed from this notice; no technical standards, platform audit protocol or outcome data are supplied.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice provides no before/after prevalence measure, comparison jurisdiction, prior enforcement baseline or platform-level audit.

brief.title: China's CAC announces a two-month campaign against misleading military content, including AI-generated fabrications
brief.why_it_matters: The notice explicitly includes AI-generated military fabrications in a cross-agency content-enforcement campaign, making it a concrete policy signal about synthetic-media governance. Its scope is limited to the enumerated conduct and named campaign; it does not establish how platforms implement the directive or whether the campaign reduces harmful content.
